text.p: Italian bonds and BTPs held firmer in late afternoon but were off the day's highs helped by U.S. T-bonds and the positive tone to German bunds, dealers said.
They added that T-bonds gained from positive signs from the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond's economic indexes which showed an economy entering 1997's third quarter with robust growth.
"This morning we were watching the Bundesbank and this afternoon the States, both have given support to BTPs and we see the uptrend continuing," said one LIFFE trader.

The move by the Bundesbank to keep the repo rate unchanged at 3.0 percent signalled unchanged monetary policy, and dampened speculation that the German central bank might allow the rate to drift higher to support the mark.

The Bank of Italy today offered to sell up to 2.0 trillion lire worth of short-term bills (BOT), and the maximum rate at the sale stood at 6.92 percent and the average rate at 6.88 percent. The offer was fully taken up and took effect today.
Dealers said some operators were already looking ahead to August CPI data due next week, which is expected to show an unchanged annual rate of 1.6 percent from July.
